2.text: “And from the Cape to that Island it is possible to go in the summer-

3.text: time in one day, in a baidara with oars; and in the wintertime, with reindeer,

4.text: also in one day. Upon this island are game of every kind, sables and martens,

5.text: foxes, polar foxes, wolves, wolverenes, polar bears, marine beavers (sea-otters).

6.text: They feed on sea-game, roots and berries, and weeds. Upon this island also

7.text: are trees of every kind, — cedar, pine, fir, larch. And the wood of those

23.text: of 1648, also mentions the (large-) toothed men living on two small islands,

24.text: evidently on the Diomede Islands. Not without interest is the mention of the

25.text: River Chukchee of the Anadyr, Nokon and his comrades, who paid tribute for

26.text: five men. Up to the present time the River Chukchee of the Middle Anadyr

27.text: pay about the same amount of tribute. Much in use among them is the

28.text: name “Nikon.” This name is of Greek origin, and belongs to the Greek-

29.text: Orthodox calendar; but it may have some connection with the name “Nokon”

30.text: of the beginning of the eighteenth century.
